title: Week 3: The Bad Town Festival

theme.name: Festival Week
theme.text: The Bad Town Festival is on. Cameras everywhere. The Press creeps up every few cards.

cards.text: The Festival's Best Marrow contest. I've grown one the size of a canoe. Linda says it's 'cheating'. It's fertiliser. Mostly. Let it enter?

right.label: Yes. Enter the marrow.
right.reaction: It took six people to carry it in. The judges looked at it. It looked back.

left.label: No. Rules are rules.
left.reaction: Bev has entered it anyway. As a 'sculpture'. It's winning Best Sculpture.

cards.text: Mayor, I tested Bev's marrow. It's still growing. About a foot an hour. It's going to fill the tent by lunch. Stop it growing?

right.label: Yes. Stop it.
right.reaction: I played it sad music. It's slowed down. It's also a bit sad now.

left.label: No. Let it grow.
left.reaction: The tent is now part of the marrow. So is a judge. He's fine. He's inside.

cards.text: Mayor, Bev's 'sculpture' is getting larger. Sculptures don't do that. I've checked the rules. Twice. Disqualify it?

right.label: Yes. Disqualify it.
right.reaction: Disqualified. Bev has staged a sit-in. On the marrow. It's still growing. She's quite high up now.

left.label: No. Art evolves.
left.reaction: The art critic from the Bugle called it 'challenging'. It ate her notebook.

cards.text: Mayor, the marrow is blocking the high street. I'd like to buy it. I'll pay a fortune. It would fix your budget. Sell it?

right.label: Yes. Sell the marrow.
right.reaction: Sold. Chad's had it moved to his garden. It's moved itself back.

left.label: No. It's Bev's.
left.reaction: Bev is delighted. She's carving a front door in it. She plans to live there.

cards.text: (Bev is standing on the marrow holding a rosette. She would like you to award Best Marrow. To her. Right now. In front of everyone.) Award it?

right.label: Yes. Best Marrow.
right.reaction: The crowd went wild. Bev made a speech. It was about fertiliser. Nobody's asking.

left.label: No. Fair's fair.
left.reaction: Best Marrow went to Timmy's potato. It's a potato. Bev is planning revenge. In vegetables.

cards.text: Boss. Battle of the Bands tonight. My band's playing. We're called The Bin Lids. We only know one song. It's mostly banging. Can we headline?

right.label: Yes. Headline.
right.reaction: They opened with banging. Closed with banging. The middle was also banging. Standing ovation.

left.label: No. Open the show.
left.reaction: They opened. They wouldn't stop. They're still on. It's been four hours.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has formed a rival band. They are called HONK. Every song is called Honk. He wants the headline slot back.) Swap the order?

right.label: Yes. Geese headline.
right.reaction: HONK played for nine minutes. It was honking. The critics called it 'raw'.

left.label: No. Randy keeps it.
left.reaction: The geese heckled the Bin Lids. In honks. It's become a duet. It's not bad.

cards.text: Mayor. The Bin Lids have been on stage for four hours. Noise complaints from three towns. One from the moon, I think. Pull the plug?

right.label: Yes. Pull the plug.
right.reaction: Plug pulled. They're not electric. They're banging bins. They're still going.

left.label: No. Let them finish.
left.reaction: They finished at dawn. Randy fell asleep in the bass drum. It's a bin.

cards.text: Mayor, a record label wants to sign the winning band. The Bugle needs to know who won. The bins or the geese. Pick a winner?

right.label: Yes. The Bin Lids.
right.reaction: Randy wept. The Bin Lids have a record deal. The record is a bin lid.

left.label: No. Call it a draw.
left.reaction: 'MAYOR DODGES MUSIC' — the Bugle. Both bands are now furious with you. They've formed a supergroup.

cards.text: Boss. The band wants to go on tour. Two weeks. Every bin in the county. I'd be away from deputy duties. Can I go?

right.label: Yes. Rock on.
right.reaction: He's gone. City Hall is very quiet. Very tidy. Nobody's eating the post. It's weird.

left.label: No. You're needed here.
left.reaction: He's staying. He's sulking. He's playing the bin in his office. All day.

cards.text: Boss. I'm back early. The tour went badly. A bin fell on Gerald. Then Gerald fell on a bin. Then we all fell in a bin. Can I have my job back?

right.label: Yes. Welcome back.
right.reaction: He's back at his desk. He's brought you a souvenir. It's a bin. From every town.

left.label: No. Not yet.
left.reaction: He's sleeping in the bin outside your window. He waves every morning. It's a lot.

cards.text: Mayor. The Great Pie Contest. My entry is a steak and kidney pie. Also it's a tyre. It's the best of both. Will you judge?

right.label: Yes. I'll judge.
right.reaction: You took a bite. It was pie. Then it was tyre. You'll be chewing until Thursday.

left.label: No. Get a real judge.
left.reaction: The real judge is Gerald. He's eating the pies. Not judging. Just eating.

cards.text: Mayor, my pie is better than Sal's pie. Mine doesn't contain any rubber. Just a little bit of whisky. And a lot of whisky. Taste it?

right.label: Yes. Taste it.
right.reaction: You can see colours you didn't know existed. Bev is giving you a wink.

left.label: No. I'm working.
left.reaction: Bev is offended. She's given the pie to Barb. Barb is singing.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has eaten forty pies. He is now the size of a small car. He would like to be declared the winner.) Declare him?

right.label: Yes. Gerald wins.
right.reaction: He won. He can't move. He's being rolled to the podium.

left.label: No. He didn't bake any.
left.reaction: He honked in protest. A small pie came out. Nobody is entering that.

cards.text: Mayor, I've analysed every pie in the contest. Three of them are pies. Two are hats. One is a cat. It's Mr Whiskers. Shall I announce this?

right.label: Yes. Announce it.
right.reaction: Mr Whiskers is furious. He was undercover. He was investigating the hats.

left.label: No. Bury the results.
left.reaction: The results were buried. Literally. In a pie. Marge has eaten the evidence.

cards.text: (Mr Whiskers is filing a complaint. He would like to be compensated for being mistaken for a pie. He would like it in fish.) Pay him in fish?

right.label: Yes. Fish it is.
right.reaction: Paid. He's eaten his fee. He's filing a second complaint. About the fish.

left.label: No. You were in the oven.
left.reaction: 'I was RESTING in the oven.' He's suing the oven. The oven has hired Randy.

cards.text: Mayor! The festival fireworks are app-controlled now. Ten thousand rockets. One button. I've called the app 'Bang'. Can I launch tonight?

right.label: Yes. Launch them.
right.reaction: The app crashed. The rockets launched anyway. All of them. At once. Sideways.

left.label: No. Use matches.
left.reaction: Old-fashioned. Brayden is crying into his laptop. The laptop is crying too.

cards.text: Mayor. Ten thousand rockets went sideways. Nobody's hurt. But the clock tower is now pink. Permanently. Arrest the app?

right.label: Yes. Arrest the app.
right.reaction: Arrested. It's in a cell. On a phone. It keeps asking for updates.

left.label: No. Pink is nice.
left.reaction: The pink clock tower is beloved. Tourists come to see it. Gerald nests in it.

cards.text: Boss. I've got the matches. I've lit one. I've lit the others. I've lit my coat. The cousins are fine. Mostly. Can I have a new coat?

right.label: Yes. New coat.
right.reaction: He chose the longest coat in Bad Town. It touches the floor. The cousins moved in immediately.

left.label: No. Patch it up.
left.reaction: He's patched it. With a bin bag. He rustles when he walks. He likes it.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. I have built my own firework. It is in the shape of a volcano. It's in my garden. Mum doesn't know. Can I light it?

right.label: Yes. With supervision.
right.reaction: Nora supervised. It was beautiful. It spelled 'TIMMY' in the sky. Then 'MUM'. Then 'SORRY'.

left.label: No. Absolutely not.
left.reaction: Disarmed. Timmy's very disappointed. He's drawing you a picture of you being disappointing.

cards.text: Mayor! 'Bang' has four million downloads. Nobody knows what it does. It's launching rockets. In other towns. Shut it down?

right.label: Yes. Shut it down.
right.reaction: Shut down. Four million people are slightly disappointed. One very happy town is no longer pink.

left.label: No. Monetise it.
left.reaction: It's the top app in the world. Nobody knows what it does. Brayden has bought a hat.

cards.text: Mayor! My parade float this year is a yacht. On wheels. With a smaller yacht on top. It won't fit down the high street. Widen the high street?

right.label: Yes. Widen it.
right.reaction: We removed a lamp post, two benches and Kevin. Temporarily. The yacht fits. Just.

left.label: No. Smaller yacht.
left.reaction: Chad has brought a smaller yacht. It's on top of a bigger yacht. He has missed the point.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole has been temporarily removed for the parade. He's on a trolley. Nobody knew you could do that. He seems confused.) Put him back?

right.label: Yes. Put Kevin back.
right.reaction: Kevin is back. People clapped. Chad's yacht hit him on the way past. Kevin seemed pleased.

left.label: No. He's in the parade.
left.reaction: Kevin has his own float now. It's a trolley. With a hole in it. He's a star.

cards.text: The PTA float is a giant papier-mâché head of the mayor. You. It was meant to be flattering. It isn't. Approve it?

right.label: Yes. I love it.
right.reaction: The giant head waved at everyone. Its eyes are different sizes. The children are terrified.

left.label: No. Fix the eyes.
left.reaction: They fixed the eyes. Now the nose is wrong. It's a work in progress.

cards.text: Mayor. The parade has jammed. The yacht is stuck at the roundabout. Reginald is the roundabout. Neither will move. Choose who moves?

right.label: Yes. Move the yacht.
right.reaction: The yacht backed up four miles. Reginald didn't notice. He's fine. He's a legend.

left.label: No. Wait for Reginald.
left.reaction: The yacht waited eleven hours. Chad's crew mutinied. They're having a picnic.

cards.text: Mayor, I'd like to end the parade by launching the yacht into the river. It's my yacht. It's my river. Kind of. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Launch it.
right.reaction: It floated for nine seconds. Then it was a submarine. The ducks are delighted. They live there now.

left.label: No. Not in the river.
left.reaction: He's parked it in the fountain. Again. It's becoming a tradition.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. For the festival I'd like to open a haunted house. In the town hall. It's already haunted. It's mostly me. Can I charge admission?

right.label: Yes. Charge them.
right.reaction: Sold out. People queued for hours. Wendy said 'boo' in a slightly cross voice. They loved it.

left.label: No. Make it free.
left.reaction: Free entry. The queue goes round the town twice. Wendy is exhausted. She can't sleep. She's a ghost.

cards.text: Wooo. The haunted house is the town's best earner in forty years. I'd like a share. I can't hold money. I'd still like it. Pay me?

right.label: Yes. Pay Wendy.
right.reaction: Paid. In coins. They fall straight through her. They're all in the basement. She's furious.

left.label: No. She's a volunteer.
left.reaction: Wendy's on strike. She just sits in a chair. Visitors call it 'scary in a new way'.

cards.text: Mayor. Readers report the haunted house is 'not scary'. They say Wendy apologises after every boo. Do something?

right.label: Yes. Scare them.
right.reaction: You hid in a wardrobe and jumped out. Bev hit you with her bag. Best review in years.

left.label: No. Nice is fine.
left.reaction: It's been rebranded 'The Nice House'. The queue is longer. Everyone gets a biscuit.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. Some other ghosts want to join. There's eleven of them. They're from 1890. They're very rude about electricity. Let them in?

right.label: Yes. Ghost party.
right.reaction: The ghosts are flicking the lights on and off. They're having the time of their deaths.

left.label: No. One ghost max.
left.reaction: They're haunting the bakery instead. Every loaf is now slightly see-through.

cards.text: Wooo. Thank you for this week. I'd like to keep the haunted house open. Forever. It's very good for my self-esteem. Can I?

right.label: Yes. Forever.
right.reaction: It's permanent. Wendy's on the town brochure. She framed it. It fell through the wall.

left.label: No. Back to normal.
left.reaction: It's closed. Wendy's floating around your office. Sighing. In a theatrical way.

cards.text: Mayor, the town is voting for a Festival Mascot. The finalists: Kevin the pothole, Pebbles the goat and Trevor the moth. Can the Bugle run the vote?

right.label: Yes. Bugle runs it.
right.reaction: The Bugle has run the vote. It's been rigged. In favour of the Bugle. The Bugle isn't running.

left.label: No. Barb runs it.
left.reaction: Barb runs it. She's arrested two voters already. For voting.

cards.text: (Pebbles has eaten every ballot paper with Kevin's name on. He looks very pleased.) Recount the votes?

right.label: Yes. Recount.
right.reaction: Recounted. With no ballots left, it's somehow a three-way tie. Pebbles is chewing smugly.

left.label: No. Let it stand.
left.reaction: Pebbles is leading. Kevin's fans are protesting. They're standing in him.

cards.text: (Trevor the moth has been seen near the ballot box. Very close to the lamp above it. He is giving it a speech about love.) Move the lamp?

right.label: Yes. Move the lamp.
right.reaction: Trevor followed the lamp. He's in the cupboard now. He's never been happier.

left.label: No. Let him campaign.
left.reaction: His speech went viral. Nobody understands it. Everyone's crying.

cards.text: Boss, it's a three-way tie. Kevin, Pebbles and Trevor. Each got exactly 412 votes. Who's breaking the tie?

right.label: Yes. You decide.
right.reaction: You picked all three. A pothole, a goat and a moth on one float. Pebbles ate the float.

left.label: No. Coin toss.
left.reaction: Randy flipped the coin. He's kept the coin. Nobody won. Randy is the mascot now.

cards.text: Boss. Festival's over. Everyone says it was the best festival ever. I'd like a speech. From you. Short. With fireworks. Do a speech?

right.label: Yes. Big speech.
right.reaction: You thanked everyone. The pink clock tower chimed. A firework went sideways. Perfect.

left.label: No. Let the town rest.
left.reaction: You didn't speak. The town went to bed. It was the quietest night in years.

cards.text: Draft law: every marrow over six feet must be registered as a building. Bev's lawyer is in the waiting room. It's Mr Whiskers. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Sign it.
right.reaction: Bev's marrow now has a postcode. It's paying council tax. It's paying more than Chad.

left.label: No. Marrows are free.
left.reaction: The marrow is untaxed. Bev is triumphant. The marrow is too.

cards.text: Draft law: no band may play for longer than its audience can stand. The Bin Lids' lawyer is a bin. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Sign it.
right.reaction: First enforced at 4am. Barb used a stopwatch and a megaphone. Then earplugs.

left.label: No. Music is free.
left.reaction: It's 6am. Somebody is still drumming. Nobody knows who. It might be the pipes.

cards.text: Draft law: pies must contain pie. Sal is weeping in the corridor. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Pie in pies.
right.reaction: Sal's pies are now 60% pie. He calls them 'diet pies'. They're selling well.

left.label: No. Pies are art.
left.reaction: Sal's opened 'Pie Without Pie'. It's a tyre in pastry. There's a waiting list.

cards.text: Draft law: fireworks may only go upwards. Brayden says this is 'anti-innovation'. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Upwards only.
right.reaction: Brayden is designing a firework that goes up, then sideways. Loophole.

left.label: No. Freedom of direction.
left.reaction: A firework went down. Into Kevin. He looks festive.

cards.text: Draft law: no yachts on land. Chad has pre-emptively sued. Twice. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Yachts to water.
right.reaction: Chad has filled his driveway with water. He's technically complying. He's very wet.

left.label: No. Land yachts are fine.
left.reaction: Three new land yachts by teatime. One is a shed with a sail.

cards.text: Draft law: ghosts must say 'boo' at a reasonable volume. Wendy has signed the petition. Twice. With one hand. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Polite boos.
right.reaction: Wendy now boos at 40 decibels. People say it's 'very respectful haunting'.

left.label: No. Boo freely.
left.reaction: Someone booed so loudly the Bugle's windows shattered. Marge has the story.

cards.text: Draft law: the Festival Mascot gets a vote on the council. Kevin, Pebbles and Trevor are all very excited. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Mascot votes.
right.reaction: First motion: Pebbles ate the agenda, Trevor voted for the lamp, Kevin abstained. As always.

left.label: No. Mascots are decor.
left.reaction: The mascot is furious. Whichever one won. Nobody can remember.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. The stilt walkers are stuck at full height. Something in Bev's fertiliser. They're getting taller. Help them down?

right.label: Yes. Get ladders.
right.reaction: Ladders weren't tall enough. We used Bev's marrow. They slid down. Gerald caught three.

left.label: No. They'll shrink.
left.reaction: They haven't shrunk. They're waving at planes. A pilot waved back.

cards.text: A legal letter. The stilt walkers are suing. They say the marrow ride was 'undignified'. They want compensation. In height. Pay it?

right.label: Yes. Pay them.
right.reaction: We've given them platform shoes. They're happy. They're also slightly taller than before.

left.label: No. They're safe.
left.reaction: They've formed a union. Tall Workers of Bad Town. Meetings are held on the roof.

cards.text: Mayor, the stilt walkers can see into every house now. They're giving the Bugle tips. It's our best week ever. Let them stay up?

right.label: Yes. Free reporting.
right.reaction: Exclusive: Doug sleeps with a spreadsheet. The Bugle sold out in nine minutes.

left.label: No. Bring them down.
left.reaction: We brought them down with a fire engine. Marge has lost her best sources.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. The band speakers are stuck on feedback. The whole town is squealing. Gerald is honking along. Cut the power?

right.label: Yes. Cut it.
right.reaction: Power's off. The squealing stopped. Gerald is still honking. That one wasn't the speakers.

left.label: No. Turn it down.
left.reaction: You turned it down. It's still squealing. Just quieter. More menacing.

cards.text: Mayor. The power cut has spoiled every fridge in town. Including mine. My fish has turned. It's now a different fish. Compensate me?

right.label: Yes. Pay Sal.
right.reaction: Sal's restocked. The 'different fish' is on the menu now. It's very popular.

left.label: No. It's festival week.
left.reaction: Sal's selling everything at half price. It's that or the river. The ducks said no.

cards.text: Mayor, the feedback is resonating with the clock tower. It's playing a note. If it goes any higher, every window in town will break. Act now?

right.label: Yes. Evacuate glass.
right.reaction: Every window was opened. The note passed through. It's in the next town now. They're furious.

left.label: No. Hold steady.
left.reaction: Every window shattered. The Bugle's headline: 'BAD TOWN GOES OPEN-PLAN'.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. Somebody entered a self-raising pie. It's still rising. It's above the treetops. It's casting a shadow. Pop it?

right.label: Yes. Pop it.
right.reaction: Popped. It rained gravy for an hour. Gerald says it's the best day of his life.

left.label: No. Let it float.
left.reaction: It's drifted out of town. The next town is now eating our pie.

cards.text: The gravy rain has soaked the school playground. The children are delighted. They're skating on it. Close the school?

right.label: Yes. Close it.
right.reaction: Closed. The children have moved the gravy skating to the park. They've invented a sport.

left.label: No. Gravy day.
left.reaction: It's a holiday now. 'Gravy Day'. Every year. The children have written a song.

cards.text: Mayor, the next town says the pie is theirs now. Finders keepers. They're calling it 'a gift from Bad Town'. Demand it back?

right.label: Yes. Get it back.
right.reaction: It's back. Slightly nibbled. With a thank-you card. And a bill for the nibbling.

left.label: No. Let them have it.
left.reaction: Relations with the next town have never been better. They've sent us a cake. It's also rising.

cards.text: Boss. Bad news. The firework smoke is so thick nobody can see. I've been the mayor twice already. Nobody noticed. Clear the smoke?

right.label: Yes. Fans everywhere.
right.reaction: Every fan is on. The smoke blew into Chad's mansion. He thinks he's on fire. He isn't. Mostly.

left.label: No. Wait it out.
left.reaction: In the smoke, Randy signed four laws. One gives raccoons the vote.

cards.text: Mayor! My mansion is full of smoke. My art collection smells of fireworks. My fish smell of fireworks. Compensate me?

right.label: Yes. Fine.
right.reaction: Paid. He's selling the smoky art as 'Festival Editions'. Double the price.

left.label: No. Open a window.
left.reaction: He opened all forty-two windows. His mansion is the coldest in town. It's very fresh.

cards.text: Boss. Raccoons can vote now. There's four hundred of us. We've all registered. We'd like to discuss your majority. Undo the law?

right.label: Yes. Undo it.
right.reaction: Undone. The raccoons are disappointed. They'd made badges.

left.label: No. Raccoon rights.
left.reaction: Four hundred new voters. They all live in Randy's coat. He's very heavy now.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. The bubble machine at the parade has jammed on. The high street is full of bubbles. Up to the second floor. Pop them?

right.label: Yes. Pop them.
right.reaction: Every officer has a pin. It took seven hours. Gerald popped half of them. With his face.

left.label: No. It's beautiful.
left.reaction: People are swimming through bubbles to work. It's the cleanest the town's ever been.

cards.text: Big Carl. I've been saving people from the bubbles all day. I'm exhausted. Can I get a medal? A small one. Bubble-shaped.

right.label: Yes. Bubble Medal.
right.reaction: It's a bubble. It popped during the ceremony. He cried. Then he saved a pigeon. Hero.

left.label: No. It's your job.
left.reaction: 'It's not even my job,' he said. 'There's no pool.' He went home in flippers.

cards.text: Mayor, a bubble has floated into the library. It has a book inside it. The book is overdue since 1972. Fine the bubble?

right.label: Yes. Fine it.
right.reaction: We fined the bubble. It popped. The book is back. The fine is outstanding. Linda's keeping a file.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: It floated out of the window. Linda watched it go. 'It'll be back,' she said. 'They always are.'

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. Sorry. I sneezed. All the lights in town went out. Ghosts don't usually sneeze. I think it's the dust. Fix the lights?

right.label: Yes. Call an electrician.
right.reaction: The electrician met Wendy. He's quit electricity. He's a ghost hunter now. Lights are back.

left.label: No. Use candles.
left.reaction: Candles everywhere. It's very romantic. Trevor has proposed to forty of them.

cards.text: Wooo. The electrician says I need to stop sneezing. I've been prescribed a ghost antihistamine. It doesn't exist. Can you invent one?

right.label: Yes. Ask Nora.
right.reaction: Nora made one. It's see-through. Wendy hasn't sneezed since. She's a bit sleepy.

left.label: No. Hold it in.
left.reaction: She's holding it in. Every time she nearly sneezes the lights flicker. It's very tense.

cards.text: (Trevor the moth has fallen in love with every candle in town. He can't choose. He's having a breakdown.) Blow some out?

right.label: Yes. Blow them out.
right.reaction: One candle left. Trevor has calmed down. He's whispering to it. It's very private.

left.label: No. Let him love.
left.reaction: He's flying between all of them. He's exhausted. He's happy. He's mostly wax.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. The festival confetti cannon has fired. Ten tonnes. All at once. The town is buried to the knees. Gerald is missing. Search?

right.label: Yes. Search for Gerald.
right.reaction: Found him. Inside the confetti. He'd built a nest. With confetti. He's refusing to leave.

left.label: No. He'll turn up.
left.reaction: He turned up. Inside the cannon. Waiting to be fired again.

cards.text: Mayor, clearing the confetti will cost the entire festival budget. Or we can just leave it. It might be a carpet now. Clear it?

right.label: Yes. Clear it.
right.reaction: Cleared. The town is clean. Gerald is living in the confetti pile at the dump. He's happy.

left.label: No. New carpet.
left.reaction: The whole town is carpeted in confetti. It's surprisingly warm. Chad's tried to sell it.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald would like to be fired from the confetti cannon. Officially. As the festival finale.) Fire him?

right.label: Yes. Fire Gerald.
right.reaction: He flew. He honked the whole way. He landed in the fountain. Chad's yacht caught him.

left.label: No. Too dangerous.
left.reaction: He's sulking in the cannon. He refuses to come out. He lives there now.

cards.text: Boss. I'm writing my memoir. 'Bins, Lies and Me'. Chapter one is about you. It's mostly true. Can I publish it?

right.label: Yes. Publish it.
right.reaction: Published. Eleven copies. He's signed all of them. Twice.

left.label: No. Let me read it.
left.reaction: You read it. In chapter one you're described as 'tall-ish'. Fair.

cards.text: Mayor, Randy's draft is in the library. Someone's added footnotes. In your handwriting. You didn't write them. Investigate?

right.label: Yes. Investigate.
right.reaction: The footnotes were Randy. He does a very good you. Suspiciously good.

left.label: No. They're good notes.
left.reaction: Linda's filed them under 'Probably Randy'. It's a big section.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle is serialising Randy's memoir. Chapter two says you're scared of ducks. You aren't. Readers believe it. Deny it?

right.label: Yes. Deny it.
right.reaction: You fed ducks on the front page. One bit you. The headline: 'TOLD YOU'.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: People now walk you past the pond. Gently. Holding your hand.

cards.text: Boss. My publisher says the memoir needs more drama. Could you fall in a river? A small one. For chapter four?

right.label: Yes. A small river.
right.reaction: You fell in a puddle. Big Carl saved you. Chapter four is mostly about Carl now.

left.label: No drama.
left.reaction: Chapter four is called 'The Boss Said No'. It's one page. It's his best work.

cards.text: Mayor, chapter three says you can't read. People now read things out to you. Slowly. Kindly. Correct the record?

right.label: Yes. Correct it.
right.reaction: You read the whole Bugle out loud on the steps. It took four hours. Bev clapped.

left.label: No. It's quite nice.
left.reaction: Doug reads you the budget every morning. With voices. It's much better with voices.

cards.text: Boss. My memoir's sold eleven copies. I bought ten. I'd like a book launch. At City Hall. With canapés. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Launch it.
right.reaction: Canapés were bins. Small, clean bins. With crisps in. A triumph.

left.label: No canapés.
left.reaction: He launched it anyway. In the car park. From a bin. With crisps.

cards.text: Boss. Chapter four's out. In it, I'm the mayor and you're my deputy. People have started calling me Mayor. Should I correct them?

right.label: Yes. Correct them.
right.reaction: He corrected them. Quietly. Once. He looked sad about it.

left.label: No. Let them.
left.reaction: 'Mayor Randy' is opening a supermarket today. He's cut the ribbon with his teeth.

cards.text: Mayor, the memoir is in the library under 'Fantasy'. Randy keeps moving it to 'History'. Move it back?

right.label: Yes. Fantasy.
right.reaction: Back to fantasy. Randy has added a dragon to chapter one. To fit in.

left.label: No. History it is.
left.reaction: It's history now. Schoolchildren are being taught that you're afraid of ducks.

cards.text: Boss. Chapter five is a blank page with your name at the top. My editor says if you sign it, you become a character. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Sign it.
right.reaction: You felt flat. Then papery. Then you were on page 212.

left.label: No. I'm real.
left.reaction: You poked yourself to check. Real. Randy looked relieved. And a bit disappointed.

cards.text: Boss. The memoir got one review. From Bev. It says 'too short'. She wants a sequel. Write it together?

right.label: Yes. Co-write it.
right.reaction: Book two: 'Bins, Lies and Us'. You wrote the chapter about bins. It's very moving.

left.label: No. One's enough.
left.reaction: He's writing it alone. It's called 'The Boss Said No Again'. It's a thriller.

cards.text: Mayor, the memoir is the town's bestseller. The last chapter is called 'The Mayor Disappears'. Fans are waiting outside to see it. Disappoint them?

right.label: Yes. Stay put.
right.reaction: You stood on the steps all day. Not disappearing. The fans left a bad review.

left.label: No. Hide for a bit.
left.reaction: You hid in the cupboard. The fans cheered. Randy is writing very fast.

cards.text: Boss. Last chapter. I want to end with a thank-you. To you. Can I use your real name? Spelled right?

right.label: Yes. Spell it right.
right.reaction: He spelled it right. First time ever. He's had it framed. The frame is a bin lid.

left.label: No. Spell it wrong.
left.reaction: He spelled it so wrong it's somebody else. They wrote to say thanks.

cards.text: (Election night. Randy holds a pen over the last page. 'Boss, if I write THE END, you stay in the book forever. As the hero.') Let him?

right.label: Yes. Write THE END.
right.reaction: The ink was still wet when you turned into a paragraph.

left.label: No. Not yet.
left.reaction: He put the pen down. 'Sequel, then,' he said. He's started already.

cards.text: Bev is sprinkling something on her marrow. It glows. Swap the bag for normal fertiliser while she's not looking.

right.label: Swapped it
right.reaction: Swapped. The marrow stopped growing. Bev doesn't know yet. She will.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: Bev caught your wrist. Ninety-seven. Grip like a vice. You're now sprinkling it for her.

cards.text: The new festival stage opens today. Gerald is waddling at the ribbon, face first. Cut it before he does!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Clean cut. The Bin Lids struck up immediately. Mostly banging.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it. Then took the stage. HONK played first. Nobody stopped them.

cards.text: Gerald is guarding the judges' pie table. Swap Sal's tyre pie for a real one while he's not looking.

right.label: Swapped it
right.reaction: Swapped. The judges loved the real pie. Sal won. He's suspicious. He's hugging the trophy.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: Gerald honked the alarm. You're holding a tyre. In front of everyone. Smile.

cards.text: The fireworks viewing platform opens tonight. Gerald is closing in on the ribbon. Snip it first!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Open. Best seats in town. A rocket went sideways and lit the ribbon too. Bonus.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: He cut it with his face. Then claimed the front row. All of it.

cards.text: Chad is sneaking a fourth yacht into the parade. Let the air out of its tyres while he's not looking.

right.label: Done it
right.reaction: Flat. The yacht is going nowhere. Chad thinks it's sabotage. It is.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: Chad caught you crouched by a yacht. He's taken a photo. It's his phone background.

cards.text: Wendy's haunted house opens today. She can't hold scissors. Gerald is racing for the ribbon. Cut it for her!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Open! Wendy woo'd with joy. The ribbon floated up and haunted the ceiling.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it and went in first. He came out very fast. Honking.

cards.text: Randy is stuffing the mascot ballot box into his coat. Grab it back while he's not looking.

right.label: Got it back
right.reaction: Got it. It was full of ballots for Randy. All in the same handwriting. His.

left.label: Caught
left.reaction: He spun round. You're holding his coat. Several cousins are looking at you.

cards.text: (The Cheese has been entered into the festival talent show. It has done nothing. It is through to the final.) Let it compete?

right.label: Yes. Let it compete.
right.reaction: It won. It did nothing. The judges said it was 'the most present act'.

left.label: No. It's a cheese.
left.reaction: It was disqualified. The vault is humming. Angrily.

cards.text: (The cheese's fans want it on tour. Every town. On a trolley. They've made T-shirts. The cheese seems keen.) Allow a cheese tour?

right.label: Yes. Cheese tour.
right.reaction: The tour sold out. The cheese came back stronger. Doug says it's been 'promoted'.

left.label: No. Stay in the vault.
left.reaction: Fans are camping outside the vault. With crackers. It's getting tense.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. Squirrel Bank. I'd like to sponsor the festival. Every sign must say 'Brought to you by Acorns'. Agreed?

right.label: Yes. Acorn-sponsored.
right.reaction: Every sign says ACORNS. The festival is now 'Acornfest'. Nobody can stop saying it.

left.label: No sponsors.
left.reaction: He's sponsored the next town's festival instead. Their signs are lovely.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. I'd like my sponsorship money back. In acorns. With interest. Squirrel interest. It compounds hourly. Pay?

right.label: Yes. Pay him.
right.reaction: Paid. Doug had to climb a tree for it. He's still up there. He likes it.

left.label: No. Negotiate.
left.reaction: You negotiated. He bit you. Gently. Legally. You owe him one acorn.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit has arrested the bouncy castle. It wouldn't stop bouncing. It's in a cell. It's still bouncing.) Release it?

right.label: Yes. Release it.
right.reaction: Released. The children cheered. Biscuit growled. He's watching it. Closely.

left.label: No. Bouncing is a crime.
left.reaction: It's serving three weeks. It's bouncing the whole time. The other prisoners love it.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit has asked for a promotion. To Chief. Barb's job. He has more arrests than her. He's brought a biscuit.) Promote him?

right.label: Yes. Chief Biscuit.
right.reaction: He's chief. Barb is his deputy. She gives him a biscuit every morning. It's in the contract.

left.label: No. Barb stays.
left.reaction: Biscuit is sulking in his basket. He's arrested the basket.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull is running the festival chip stall. Every chip on it was stolen. The prices are very fair.) Shut it down?

right.label: Yes. Shut it.
right.reaction: Shut. Lorraine has relocated to your roof. With the chips. She's open till late.

left.label: No. Fair prices.
left.reaction: Best-selling stall at the festival. Everyone's chips are going missing. Then on sale.

cards.text: Mayor. That seagull is selling my chips. Back to me. At a discount. I've bought them twice. Do something!

right.label: Yes. Back Sal.
right.reaction: Lorraine has called a truce. She now steals only from Chad. Sal is thrilled. Chad is livid.

left.label: No. Free market.
left.reaction: Sal has hired Lorraine. To steal from the next town's chip shop. Business is booming.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot would like to host the festival quiz. At 3am. 'It's when I'm sharpest.') Allow the night quiz?

right.label: Yes. Night quiz.
right.reaction: Four contestants. Three were asleep. Hoot won his own quiz. He's very proud.

left.label: No. Daytime only.
left.reaction: He held it at noon. Asleep. The answer to every question was 'who'. Most were right.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. Professor Hoot asked me 'who?' in the quiz. I said 'who what?'. He said 'exactly'. Did I win?

right.label: Yes. Timmy wins.
right.reaction: Timmy won. He's been made Assistant Owl. He's practising sitting still.

left.label: No. Nobody won.
left.reaction: Hoot has taken the trophy home. It's in his nest. With a mouse. Sort of a gift.

cards.text: (Toby the oak tree would like to be the festival maypole. Ribbons tied to him. Everyone dancing round. He's very excited.) Let him?

right.label: Yes. Dance round Toby.
right.reaction: Everybody danced. Toby rustled with joy. Several squirrels joined in.

left.label: No. We have a pole.
left.reaction: He's dropped every leaf on the real maypole. One go. Very precise.

cards.text: Mayor, after the dancing, Toby has grown three feet. All upwards. He's now taller than the clock tower. Trim him?

right.label: Yes. A light trim.
right.reaction: Trimmed. He's sulking. Leaves everywhere. Mostly on Doug's car.

left.label: No. Let him tower.
left.reaction: Bad Town's new tallest landmark. Gerald lives at the top. It's a goose penthouse.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. I've swallowed the festival lost property. Two umbrellas, a trumpet and a small child's shoe. Shall I return them?

right.label: Yes, please.
right.reaction: He coughed it all up. Plus a second trumpet. Nobody knows whose that is.

left.label: No. Keep them safe.
left.reaction: He's very lumpy. He plays the trumpet when he walks. Not on purpose.

cards.text: Mayor, the second trumpet Mr Flaps coughed up is from 1952. It's library property. It's overdue. Fine the pelican?

right.label: Yes. Fine him.
right.reaction: He paid in fish. Linda has accepted. The library smells of fish now.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: The trumpet has been returned. The library has started a brass section.

cards.text: (Pebbles is judging the festival flower show. He has eaten three entries. He says they were below standard.) Remove him?

right.label: Yes. Remove him.
right.reaction: Removed. He's eaten the 'Judges Only' sign on his way out.

left.label: No. He has taste.
left.reaction: The remaining entrants are terrified. Linda's rose has been hidden in her coat.

cards.text: The PTA would like to complain. Pebbles has eaten the flower show trophy. It was a rosette. And a plinth. Do something?

right.label: Yes. New trophy.
right.reaction: The new trophy is made of metal. Pebbles has looked at it. He's thinking.

left.label: No. It's a goat.
left.reaction: The PTA has passed a motion: 'No goats'. Pebbles ate the motion.

cards.text: (Clive the traffic cone has had his face painted at the festival. He has a face now. It's smiling. Nobody's sure they like it.) Wash it off?

right.label: Yes. Wash it off.
right.reaction: Washed off. He looks the same. But somehow sadder.

left.label: No. He looks happy.
left.reaction: His approval rating has gone up. It's the face. The face is working.

cards.text: Mayor, readers are saying Clive looked happier with a face. There's a petition. 'Faces For Cones.' It has 900 names. Respond?

right.label: Yes. Faces for cones.
right.reaction: Every cone in town has a face. They're all smiling. Driving is unsettling now.

left.label: No. Cones are cones.
left.reaction: 900 people have drawn faces on their own cones. At home. In protest.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine is selling festival souvenirs. They're all crisps shaped like your face. Salt and vinegar.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. It's flattering.
right.reaction: They sold out. People are eating your face. It's unsettling. It's profitable.

left.label: No. Cease and desist.
left.reaction: He's switched to crisps shaped like Randy. Randy has bought all of them.

cards.text: (Reginald the tortoise has entered the festival fun run. He started last year. He's on the home straight.) Hold the finish line open?

right.label: Yes. Wait for him.
right.reaction: He crossed it at 4am. Six people stayed up. They cried. He didn't notice.

left.label: No. It's over.
left.reaction: They took the finish line down. He's still running. He'll finish at the next one.

cards.text: Mayor! Reginald finished! Officially he came last. But he's also first in next year's race. He started already. Medal?

right.label: Yes. Two medals.
right.reaction: Two medals. One for last year, one for next year. He's wearing both. Slowly.

left.label: No. One race at a time.
left.reaction: He's had a word with Coach. Very slowly. It took the whole afternoon.

cards.text: Big Carl. I've set up a lifeguard tower next to the duck pond. The ducks say they feel watched. I am watching them. Okay?

right.label: Yes. Watch the ducks.
right.reaction: A duckling fell in. Carl dived. It was already swimming. He brought it back anyway.

left.label: No. Ducks can swim.
left.reaction: 'That's what they want you to think,' he said. He's still there. With binoculars.

cards.text: (Marcel the mime has mimed a wall around the main festival stage. Nobody can get in. People are walking into it.) Make him stop?

right.label: Yes. Down with the wall.
right.reaction: He mimed a door. It's locked. He's mimed losing the key. He's very good.

left.label: No. It's performance.
left.reaction: Critics say it's his best wall yet. Twenty people have bumped into it.

cards.text: Mayor. People are queuing at Marcel's mimed door. He's charging for an invisible key. People are paying. Is this a crime?

right.label: Yes. Arrest him.
right.reaction: Arrested. He's mimed a cell. He's in it. He's mimed the cell being very small.

left.label: No. It's art.
left.reaction: He's sold 400 invisible keys. Doug has asked for invisible tax.

cards.text: (Mr Whiskers Esq. would like a festival tent for cats only. Dogs may enter if they have a lawyer. He is a lawyer.) Approve?

right.label: Yes. Cats only.
right.reaction: Inspector Biscuit applied for entry. Mr Whiskers is representing him. It's complicated.

left.label: No. Everyone's welcome.
left.reaction: He's filed a complaint. On the festival programme. In paw print.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole has become the festival's unofficial wishing well. People are throwing coins in him. He seems moved.) Collect the coins?

right.label: Yes. For the town.
right.reaction: £43.12 and a button. Doug kissed the button. Kevin looks a bit emptier.

left.label: No. They're Kevin's.
left.reaction: Kevin is the richest pothole in the county. Nobody knows what he'll do with it. He's a hole.

cards.text: (Trevor the moth would like the front row for the fireworks. He's been warned. He says he 'knows what he's doing'.) Give him the front row?

right.label: Yes. Front row.
right.reaction: He watched every rocket. He tried to marry three of them. He's fine. Slightly singed. Very happy.

left.label: No. Back row.
left.reaction: He watched from the back. Through tears. And a lamp. He's moved on. To the lamp.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot has sent every child home from school. It's 9am. He says it's the middle of the night.) Overrule him?

right.label: Yes. Back to school.
right.reaction: Back to school. Hoot is asleep at his desk. The children are teaching themselves. It's going well.

left.label: No. Night school.
left.reaction: The children are thrilled. Lessons start at 9pm. Owls are now attending.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. I would like to be festival director. I have a clipboard. I have made a schedule. It is mostly bouncy castle. Yes?

right.label: Yes. Director Timmy.
right.reaction: Eleven bouncy castles. One is inside another. Timmy's never been prouder.

left.label: No. Assistant director.
left.reaction: He's accepted. He's added a twelfth bouncy castle to your office.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle wants to rate the festival toilets. Out of ten. On the front page. Every day. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Rate them.
right.reaction: Day one: 2/10. Day two: 4/10. Day three: 'improving'. Sal is furious. His tent is a toilet now.

left.label: No. Some dignity.
left.reaction: They're rating them anyway. Anonymously. The reviewer is clearly Bev.

cards.text: Mayor! Festival tug of war! Bad Town against the geese. The geese have agreed. Gerald has been training. Approve it?

right.label: Yes. Pull!
right.reaction: The geese won. Easily. They didn't pull. They just honked. Everyone let go.

left.label: No. Somebody gets bitten.
left.reaction: Coach is devastated. He's challenged the geese to chess instead. They ate the pieces.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald would like a rematch. With the rope tied to your car.) Allow the rematch?

right.label: Yes. Rematch.
right.reaction: Gerald won again. Your car is in the pond. He's sitting on it. Victory.

left.label: No. You won.
left.reaction: He's honking 'rematch' outside your window. Every night. Rhythmically.

cards.text: Mayor, my judging robot has scored every festival entry 6 out of 10. Including the sky. And the marrow. And me. Keep it?

right.label: Yes. Fair is fair.
right.reaction: The robot gave the mayor a 6. You've never felt more average. It's freeing.

left.label: No. Turn it off.
left.reaction: Turned off. It gave being turned off a 6. Nora's moved on. She's building a 7.

cards.text: Mayor. My festival stall is selling 'tyre fries'. They're fries. Shaped like tyres. Mostly. Will you try one?

right.label: Yes. Try one.
right.reaction: It was a fry. Then a tyre. Then a fry again. Sal's sold four thousand.

left.label: No. Not today.
left.reaction: Sal's offered one to Gerald. Gerald ate the stall.

cards.text: Mayor. I'd like to charge festival entry. Two pence. I've done the maths. It would fix everything. Charge it?

right.label: Yes. Two pence.
right.reaction: Two pence each. Doug made £41. He wept with joy. Then reality.

left.label: No. Free festival.
left.reaction: Free entry. Doug's taking donations in a jar. The jar has gone missing. Randy.

cards.text: Mayor! I want to put Wi-Fi in the duck pond. Smart ducks. Connected ducks. Duck-as-a-service. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Smart ducks.
right.reaction: The ducks are online. They've set up a group chat. You're not in it.

left.label: No. Analogue ducks.
left.reaction: Brayden's crying again. The ducks have comforted him. Analogue-ly.

cards.text: Crime is up. Someone's stealing festival bunting. All of it. One flag at a time. I can't keep up. Hire more officers?

right.label: Yes. More officers.
right.reaction: Four new officers. They're all Randy's cousins. In hats.

left.label: No. Do your best.
left.reaction: Barb is guarding the bunting personally. With a deck chair. And a flask.

cards.text: There's a protest outside City Hall. They're angry about the festival noise. They've brought a brass band. Talk to them?

right.label: Yes. Talk to them.
right.reaction: You listened. They played you a song. It was quite good, actually.

left.label: No. Wait it out.
left.reaction: They've joined the festival. They're on the main stage. Protesting. Loudly.

cards.text: Mayor. The festival has spent all our money. I've been selling my own cardigans. Sell the festival stage?

right.label: Yes. Sell the stage.
right.reaction: Sold. The bands play in the car park now. Acoustics are 'interesting'.

left.label: No. Tax the stalls.
left.reaction: Taxed. Sal is paying in tyres. Doug can't bank tyres. He's tried.

cards.text: Business is booming! I'd like to buy the festival. Name and all. 'ChadFest'. It's catchy. Sell it?

right.label: Yes. ChadFest.
right.reaction: ChadFest. Tickets are £400. Chad is the only one inside. He's having a great time.

left.label: No.
left.reaction: He's bought the field next door. He's having a bigger festival. Just him. Very loud.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle loves you so much we've put you on every page. The crossword. The horoscopes. The weather. Tone it down?

right.label: Yes. Tone it down.
right.reaction: You're back to just the front page. And page four. Marge is grieving.

left.label: No. More of me.
left.reaction: The Bugle is now 40 pages of your face. Readers are starting to worry.

cards.text: Boss. I've opened a festival stall. It's my coat. Hanging up. People pay to look inside. Can I keep it open?

right.label: Yes. Keep it open.
right.reaction: Queue round the block. Nobody will say what's in there. Everybody comes out changed.

left.label: No. Shut the coat.
left.reaction: Shut. The cousins are disappointed. They'd rehearsed.

cards.text: Mayor. Three people went into Randy's coat stall. Two came out. The third has a job in there now. Is that legal?

right.label: Yes. It's employment.
right.reaction: He's very happy. Good pension. Raccoon dental.

left.label: No. Get him out.
left.reaction: Rescued. He's asking to go back in. He misses the cousins.

cards.text: Mayor, I'd like to DJ at the festival. I've got records. Mostly brass bands. One by a man who whistles. Give me a slot?

right.label: Yes. DJ Bev.
right.reaction: She played the whistling man for three hours. The crowd went feral.

left.label: No. We have DJs.
left.reaction: She's DJing from her scooter. Driving round the festival. Loudly.

cards.text: Mayor, DJ Bev has been booked for a festival in the city. They want her for the main stage. She's ninety-seven. Let her go?

right.label: Yes. Go, Bev.
right.reaction: She headlined. Forty thousand people whistled along. She's back by Tuesday. Hungover.

left.label: No. Stay local.
left.reaction: She's cancelled. Forty thousand people are very disappointed. One whistling man most of all.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. Festival forecast: a hundred percent chance of rain. So, a hundred percent chance of sun. I'm never right. Cancel the umbrellas?

right.label: Yes. Trust Steve.
right.reaction: It was sunny. Steve was wrong, which was right. He's very confused about it.

left.label: No. Bring umbrellas.
left.reaction: It was sunny. Everyone carried an umbrella for nothing. Steve feels vindicated. Somehow.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. I got it right yesterday by being wrong. I'm worried I'll get it right on purpose. Should I quit?

right.label: Yes. Quit while ahead.
right.reaction: He's quit. The new weatherman is a seaweed. It's very accurate. Nobody likes it.

left.label: No. Keep being wrong.
left.reaction: He's back. Wrong as ever. Everybody's relieved.

cards.text: Mayor, the library would like a Quiet Zone at the festival. No music. No talking. No geese. Approve it?

right.label: Yes. Quiet Zone.
right.reaction: It's the most popular tent at the festival. People sleep there. One man proposed. In mime.

left.label: No. It's a festival.
left.reaction: Linda's shushing the main stage. From the side. It's working, oddly.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has entered the Quiet Zone. He is trying very hard. He is vibrating.) Let him stay?

right.label: Yes. He's trying.
right.reaction: He lasted eleven minutes. Then one enormous honk. Standing ovation. Silently.

left.label: No. Out.
left.reaction: He left. He honked outside the tent for an hour. Then went back in. Calmer.

cards.text: Mayor! Festival sack race! I've entered the town council. You're in a sack. Doug's in a sack. Randy is already in his sack. Hop?

right.label: Yes. Hop.
right.reaction: You came second. To Doug. He's never won anything. He's had the sack framed.

left.label: No. Dignity.
left.reaction: You watched. Randy won. His sack was his coat. Disqualified. He's appealing.

cards.text: Mayor. I won the sack race. I'd like the prize money. It's £2. It's in the budget. I've checked. Can I have it?

right.label: Yes. You earned it.
right.reaction: Doug bought a sandwich. He ate it slowly. It was the best day of his life.

left.label: No. Budget's tight.
left.reaction: He's put the £2 back in the budget. He visits it.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull is circling the festival ice cream van. She has friends. Forty of them. They're in formation.) Guard the van?

right.label: Yes. Guard it.
right.reaction: Barb stood guard. Lorraine waited. Barb blinked. The van is empty now.

left.label: No. Ice cream for all.
left.reaction: Forty seagulls ate forty cones. Lorraine left a tip. It's a chip.

cards.text: Mayor. That seagull has stolen my ice cream van. The whole van. It's on the roof of the church. How?

right.label: Yes. Get it down.
right.reaction: It took a crane and a vicar. Lorraine watched from the steeple. Clapping. With wings.

left.label: No. It's a landmark.
left.reaction: Ice cream on the church roof. Sal sells cones by bucket on a rope. Business is booming.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. I lost my balloon. It's a dinosaur. It's very high up. It's above the clock tower. Can you get it back?

right.label: Yes. Get the balloon.
right.reaction: Big Carl climbed the clock tower. Got the balloon. Got stuck. Timmy rescued him.

left.label: No. It's gone now.
left.reaction: Timmy watched it go. He waved. He said 'it's free now'. Everyone cried.

cards.text: Big Carl. I was rescued by an eight-year-old. On a clock tower. In flippers. Can we not tell anyone?

right.label: Yes. It never happened.
right.reaction: Nobody will ever know. Except the Bugle. They have photographs. Lots.

left.label: No. You're a hero.
left.reaction: Front page: 'TIMMY SAVES CARL'. Carl has framed it. Under protest.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. A ghost hunter has come to the festival. He's hunting me. With a hoover. Can you have a word?

right.label: Yes. Have a word.
right.reaction: You had a word. He's switched to hunting dust. Wendy is very grateful.

left.label: No. Hide in the attic.
left.reaction: She hid. He hoovered the attic. She's in the hoover now. She likes it. It's cosy.

cards.text: Wooo. The ghost hunter and I have become friends. He'd like to stay in Bad Town. Haunted. By me. Can he?

right.label: Yes. Let him stay.
right.reaction: He's moved in. Wendy haunts him gently. Every morning. With a cup of tea.

left.label: No. He has a home.
left.reaction: He's left. Wendy waved. He waved back. At the wrong ghost.

cards.text: Mayor! The Bang app needs permission to 'access everything'. Including the treasury. And the rockets. Just tap allow?

right.label: Yes. Allow.
right.reaction: The app said 'thank you'. Then it said 'launching everything'.

left.label: No. Deny.
left.reaction: Denied. The app sulked. It launched one small, sad rocket.

cards.text: Boss. The Bin Lids want to stage-dive from the clock tower. Into the crowd. The crowd hasn't been told. Ban stage diving?

right.label: Yes. Ban it.
right.reaction: Banned. Randy dived anyway. Into a bin. A perfect landing.

left.label: No. I'll dive first.
left.reaction: You dived. The crowd parted. Politely.

cards.text: Mayor, taste my pie. The secret ingredient came with a label saying 'DO NOT EAT'. I've taken the label off. Taste?

right.label: Yes. A big bite.
right.reaction: It was delicious. Then it was Thursday.

left.label: No. I'm full.
left.reaction: Bev fed it to Gerald. He's still asleep. Peacefully. Snoring.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. I made a big firework. It says DO NOT HOLD on the side. Can you hold it while I light it? Please?

right.label: Yes. I'll hold it.
right.reaction: You held it. You saw the whole festival from above. Then the next town.

left.label: No. Put it down.
left.reaction: Nora lit it. From very far away. It spelled TIMMY in the sky. Then SORRY.

cards.text: Mayor! Ride on the very top of my parade yacht! It's eighty feet tall. The bridge ahead is forty. It's fine, I think. Climb up?

right.label: Yes. Climb up.
right.reaction: The yacht fitted under the bridge. You did not.

left.label: No. I'll walk.
left.reaction: You walked. The top of the yacht stayed at the bridge. With Chad on it.

cards.text: Wooo. Mayor. The other ghosts want you to stay the night. In the room marked 'FOREVER'. Or you could go home. Go home?

right.label: Yes. Go home.
right.reaction: You went home. The door marked FOREVER closed itself. Quietly. Disappointed.

left.label: No. One night.
left.reaction: It said forever. It meant forever.

cards.text: Mayor. Pebbles has eaten tonight's ballot box. If we don't re-run the vote, his result stands, and the goat only ever votes for the goat. Re-run it?

right.label: Yes. Re-run it.
right.reaction: Re-run by hand. Pebbles watched. Hungrily. Nobody turned their back.

left.label: No. Wait for the goat.
left.reaction: You waited. The ballots came back. The readable ones all said GOAT.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. I'd like to hold a festival race. Squirrels only. The prize is the town's oak tree. Toby has not been consulted. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Squirrel race.
right.reaction: Four hundred squirrels. One tree. Toby has asked for a lawyer.

left.label: No. Toby's not a prize.
left.reaction: Mr Nutkins has offered Toby a loan instead. Toby is thinking about it.

cards.text: (Toby the oak tree is covered in squirrels. All of them claim to have won. He'd like them off.) Clear the tree?

right.label: Yes. Clear him.
right.reaction: Cleared. Toby has shaken himself. Twice. Very dignified.

left.label: No. Let them settle.
left.reaction: They've formed a government in his branches. It's very hierarchical.

cards.text: (Gary the vending machine has learned to play music. One song. Over and over. It's quite catchy.) Let him play at the festival?

right.label: Yes. DJ Gary.
right.reaction: Four hours of one song. People are dancing. People are crying. Both.

left.label: No. Unplug the music.
left.reaction: He's playing it quieter. You can still hear it. You'll hear it in your sleep.

cards.text: (Inspector Biscuit has found a lost child at the festival. It's Timmy. He wasn't lost. Biscuit won't let go of his sleeve.) Intervene?

right.label: Yes. Free Timmy.
right.reaction: Timmy is free. Biscuit has found him again. Four times. It's a game now.

left.label: No. Biscuit's working.
left.reaction: Biscuit has returned Timmy to his mum. She wasn't lost either. She's been returned too.

cards.text: Dear Mayor. The police dog keeps finding me. I'm hiding in the bouncy castle. He's bouncing. Can I be lost on purpose?

right.label: Yes. Hide away.
right.reaction: Biscuit found him in eleven seconds. They've been made official festival partners.

left.label: No. Stay found.
left.reaction: Timmy has been found. Permanently. He has a badge. It says 'FOUND'.

cards.text: Mayor, the Bugle is rating every festival stall out of ten. Sal got a two. Sal is outside with a tyre. Print the ratings?

right.label: Yes. Print them.
right.reaction: Printed. Sal has eaten his review. Out of protest. And a little hunger.

left.label: No. Be kind.
left.reaction: Marge printed a 'Kindness Special'. Everything got a seven. Readers are suspicious.

cards.text: Mayor. I got a two from the Bugle. I'd like a recount. Done by someone who's eaten a tyre pie. Arrange it?

right.label: Yes. A fair recount.
right.reaction: Re-rated by Gerald. Ten out of ten. He ate the stall. And the review.

left.label: No. A two is a two.
left.reaction: Sal has renamed his stall 'TWO OUT OF TEN'. It's become a cult hit.

cards.text: (Lorraine the seagull has entered the parade. Forty seagulls. In formation. Each holding a chip. They want the front.) Let them lead?

right.label: Yes. Gulls first.
right.reaction: They led. They dropped every chip on Chad's yacht. Twice. Crowd loved it.

left.label: No. Back of the parade.
left.reaction: At the back, they stole the parade's sandwiches. All of them. In formation.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. Festival post is very heavy. Four thousand postcards of the giant marrow. I can carry two thousand. Two trips?

right.label: Yes. Two trips.
right.reaction: Two trips. Every postcard arrived. Slightly damp. The marrow looks bigger in them.

left.label: No. One trip.
left.reaction: He swallowed four thousand. He's very round. He's delivering by rolling.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. One of the marrow postcards was addressed to the marrow. From Bev. Shall I deliver it?

right.label: Yes. Deliver it.
right.reaction: He posted it into the marrow. It's been read. Somehow. Bev's marrow seems happier.

left.label: No. Return to sender.
left.reaction: Returned. Bev has re-sent it. By hand. Into the marrow.

cards.text: (Reginald the tortoise has wandered onto the main stage during the headline act. He's moving towards the microphone.) Let him?

right.label: Yes. His moment.
right.reaction: He reached the microphone at 2am. He said nothing. Ovation.

left.label: No. Carry him off.
left.reaction: Carried off. He's walking back on. Slowly. Determinedly. He'll arrive on Tuesday.

cards.text: Boss. The Bin Lids want Reginald in the band. On drums. He'd hit one drum per hour. Very steady. Can he join?

right.label: Yes. Reginald on drums.
right.reaction: One beat per hour. The slowest song ever written. It's still going.

left.label: No. Too slow.
left.reaction: He's started his own band. Solo. It's very relaxing. He's selling out.

cards.text: The PTA's face-painting tent has run out of paint. They're using the Bugle's ink. Every child now looks like a headline. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. News faces.
right.reaction: Timmy's face says 'MAYOR IN CRISIS'. He's very proud of it.

left.label: No. Close the tent.
left.reaction: Closed. The children have painted each other with jam. It's worse. It's stickier.

cards.text: Mayor, a child's face reading 'MAYOR IN CRISIS' has gone viral. It's now the Bugle's best seller. Respond?

right.label: Yes. Paint your own.
right.reaction: Your face now reads 'NO CRISIS'. It's on page one. It looks like a crisis.

left.label: No comment.
left.reaction: 'MAYOR NO COMMENT ON FACE' is page one. The face is page two.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot has asked to watch the fireworks. From inside the fireworks shed. 'It's quieter.') Let him?

right.label: Yes. He's an owl.
right.reaction: He watched. Every firework lit at once. Hoot didn't blink. Hoot never blinks.

left.label: No. Outside.
left.reaction: He watched from outside. Upside down. From a lamp post. He said it was 'adequate'.

cards.text: (The 1987 cheese has been entered into the festival's 'Best Local Produce'. Nobody entered it. It's on the table.) Let it compete?

right.label: Yes. Let it compete.
right.reaction: It won. The judges couldn't say why. One judge is still staring at it.

left.label: No. Back to the vault.
left.reaction: It's back in the vault. The trophy has gone missing. Also into the vault.

cards.text: (The cheese won 'Best Local Produce'. The prize is £50. A note under the vault door says PAY ME. INTO THE VAULT.) Pay the cheese?

right.label: Yes. Pay the cheese.
right.reaction: Paid. The £50 vanished. The vault is warmer. Doug won't go near it.

left.label: No. Cheese can't earn.
left.reaction: Doug's office now smells of 1987. Doug is negotiating.

cards.text: (Marcel the mime has challenged Bev to a mime battle. Bev has accepted. She's never mimed before. She's very loud.) Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Mime off.
right.reaction: Bev mimed a scooter crash. With sound effects. Marcel conceded.

left.label: No. Too dangerous.
left.reaction: Marcel mimed being disappointed. Bev mimed not caring. Both very good.

cards.text: (Marcel would like a rematch. He's been practising. He's mimed a gym. And a trainer. And a protein shake.) Rematch?

right.label: Yes. Rematch.
right.reaction: Marcel won. Bev mimed a protest. It was very convincing. People joined in.

left.label: No. It's over.
left.reaction: He's miming a sulk. He's been miming it for three days. Very committed.

cards.text: (Clive the traffic cone has been placed at the festival entrance. People think he's directing them. He's very good at it.) Make it official?

right.label: Yes. Steward Clive.
right.reaction: Best-organised festival in history. Clive hasn't moved. He doesn't need to.

left.label: No. He's a cone.
left.reaction: Without Clive the queue went in nine directions. Somebody put him back.

cards.text: Mayor! Egg and spoon race! Gerald has entered. With his own egg. He laid it this morning. He says. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Let him race.
right.reaction: He won. He ate the spoon. Nobody checked the egg.

left.label: No. Shop eggs only.
left.reaction: Gerald has filed a complaint. With his egg. On your desk.

cards.text: Mayor, the library's festival book stall has sold one book. To Randy. It was his own memoir. He's returning it. For a refund. Refund?

right.label: Yes. Refund him.
right.reaction: Refunded. He's bought it again. He likes the transaction.

left.label: No. No refunds.
left.reaction: He's donated it back. With a signature. The library now owns a signed copy. It's worth 3p.

cards.text: Stormy Steve. I've forecast sun for the festival finale. So, obviously, bring umbrellas. Do I announce that?

right.label: Yes. Announce it.
right.reaction: Everyone brought umbrellas. It was sunny. Steve has never been more wrong. Or more popular.

left.label: No. Say nothing.
left.reaction: It rained. Nobody had umbrellas. Steve was right by accident. He's in shock.

cards.text: Mayor! Drone light show! Forty drones! Spelling 'BAD TOWN' in the sky! Approve the launch?

right.label: Yes. Launch them.
right.reaction: They spelled 'BAD TOWM'. Close enough. Gerald attacked three. He won.

left.label: No. Stars are fine.
left.reaction: Brayden has launched one drone. It spells 'SAD'. It's hovering over your house.

cards.text: Mayor, the festival rides are too slow. I'd like to ride the big wheel standing up. On top. Holding a sandwich. Permission?

right.label: Yes. Up you go.
right.reaction: She did a full rotation. Ate the sandwich at the top. Waved. Big Carl fainted.

left.label: No. Sit down, Bev.
left.reaction: She sat. On the operator. The wheel went faster. Everyone screamed. Joyfully.

cards.text: Boss. I've found the festival's lost-property box. There's a trumpet, a wig and a full-size canoe. Can I keep the canoe?

right.label: Yes. Keep it.
right.reaction: He's paddling the canoe down the high street. On wheels. It's very slow.

left.label: No. Hand it in.
left.reaction: Handed in. It was Bev's. She's furious it was lost. She lost it on purpose.

cards.text: Mayor, I'd like a VIP zone at the festival. Velvet rope. Free champagne. Just for me. Approve it?

right.label: Yes. Chad's zone.
right.reaction: He's alone in it. With champagne. Waving at everyone. Nobody waves back. He's thrilled.

left.label: No. Everyone's a VIP.
left.reaction: Everyone's a VIP. Chad has made a VVIP zone. It's his car.

cards.text: Mayor. Lost property has handed in a lost police officer. It's me. I got lost in the hall of mirrors. Can someone come and get me?

right.label: Yes. Rescue Barb.
right.reaction: Rescued. She arrested eleven reflections on the way out. All for looking at her.

left.label: No. Follow the signs.
left.reaction: She followed the signs. They were mirrors. She's still in there. She's set up an office.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has opened a festival stall. It's called 'BREAD FOR GEESE'. It is a goose standing next to bread. Him.) Allow?

right.label: Yes. Bread for geese.
right.reaction: Best-selling stall. Every goose in town is queueing. They're paying in feathers.

left.label: No. Unlicensed bread.
left.reaction: He has eaten the stock. And the stall. He's now a goose standing next to nothing.

cards.text: (Mr Whiskers Esq. would like the festival's lost-cat announcement read in full. He is not lost. He'd just like to be announced.) Announce him?

right.label: Yes. Announce him.
right.reaction: 'Mr Whiskers, Esquire, is not lost.' Applause. He's been announced four more times.

left.label: No. Only lost cats.
left.reaction: He's got himself lost. On purpose. In the VIP zone. Chad is allergic.

cards.text: Mayor. I'd like to enter the festival talent show. I'll be reading the budget. Aloud. With feeling. May I?

right.label: Yes. Go on, Doug.
right.reaction: He cried during the treasury section. So did the audience. He came second. To the cheese.

left.label: No. Keep it private.
left.reaction: He read it to himself. In a cupboard. With feeling.

cards.text: The PTA would like to sell homemade jam at the festival. Every jar is labelled 'JAM (PROBABLY)'. Approve?

right.label: Yes. Probably jam.
right.reaction: It was jam. Mostly. One jar was soup. It sold out first.

left.label: No. Label it properly.
left.reaction: New labels: 'JAM (DEFINITELY, PROBABLY)'. Pam stands by it.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole has been decorated with festival bunting. He looks very festive. People are posing in him.) Charge for photos?

right.label: Yes. Photo fee.
right.reaction: 50p a photo. Kevin has made more than the festival. He's still a hole.

left.label: No. Free Kevin.
left.reaction: Free photos. Four thousand of them. Kevin is the most photographed hole in the county.

cards.text: Mayor, I've made a glow stick that never stops glowing. It also hums. And it's warm. Hand them out at the festival?

right.label: Yes. Hand them out.
right.reaction: The whole festival glows. And hums. The cheese has started humming back.

left.label: No. Lock them up.
left.reaction: Locked in the vault. With the cheese. The vault is glowing now. Doug won't go in.

cards.text: (Marcel the mime would like to headline the festival. The act is 'Man Trapped in Festival'. It's four hours long.) Book him?

right.label: Yes. Headline slot.
right.reaction: Four hours of silence. The Bugle called it 'a triumph'. Nobody else is sure.

left.label: No. Five minutes.
left.reaction: Five minutes. He mimed an hour into it. Somehow it felt longer.

cards.text: Mayor, Marcel's show is so quiet I can't sell anything. Nobody dares open a crisp packet. Can I put a speaker next to him?

right.label: Yes. A speaker.
right.reaction: Chad's speaker played his advert over Marcel. Marcel mimed fainting. Encore.

left.label: No. Respect the art.
left.reaction: Chad has started miming his adverts. He's terrible at it. Sales are up.

cards.text: (Marcel is outside your office, miming being very, very sad. He's very good at it. People are stopping to cry.) Give him more time?

right.label: Yes. An hour, then.
right.reaction: An hour. He used all of it to mime saying thank you. It was lovely.

left.label: No. Five minutes.
left.reaction: He's mimed a wall around your office. Nobody can get in. Nobody tries.

cards.text: (Marcel's final act: he mimes the whole festival backwards. He'd like you on stage. You'd be the ribbon.) Go on stage?

right.label: Yes. Be the ribbon.
right.reaction: You stood still for nine minutes. Then he mimed cutting you. Standing ovation.

left.label: No. Stage fright.
left.reaction: Marcel used an invisible mayor instead. Critics say it was more convincing.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot is running the festival pub quiz. Every answer so far has been 'who'. He says that's correct.) Let him carry on?

right.label: Yes. Keep quizzing.
right.reaction: 'Who wrote Hamlet?' 'Who.' 'Correct.' The pub has never been happier.

left.label: No. Normal answers.
left.reaction: Hoot has refused to blink until it's fixed. It's very unsettling.

cards.text: Mayor, I've won the owl quiz four times. Answer was 'who' each time. Hoot says I'm cheating. I'm not. I'm just quick. Back me?

right.label: Yes. Bev wins.
right.reaction: Bev holds the trophy. It's a mouse. A real one. It's very upset.

left.label: No. Disqualify her.
left.reaction: Bev is starting her own quiz. Every answer is 'Bev'. It's very popular.

cards.text: Mayor, Hoot has stopped blinking. He's staring at the library. Since Tuesday. Can we let him do 'who' answers again?

right.label: Yes. Back to 'who'.
right.reaction: He blinked. The whole library cheered. Linda shushed them. Tearfully.

left.label: No. Stand firm.
left.reaction: The Bugle has a live Hoot Blink Watch. Day four. No blink.

cards.text: (Final round. Hoot's question: 'Who is the best mayor in Bad Town?' He's staring at you. Waiting.) Answer 'who'?

right.label: Yes. 'Who.'
right.reaction: 'Correct.' You won the quiz. The prize is a book called 'Who'. All 300 pages.

left.label: No. Say your name.
left.reaction: 'Incorrect.' Hoot has awarded the point to Gerald. Gerald wasn't playing.

cards.text: (Trevor the moth has heard about the festival lantern parade. All of it. Hundreds of lanterns. He's very emotional.) Invite him?

right.label: Yes. Trevor's parade.
right.reaction: He's at the front. He's crying. A moth can cry. You didn't know that.

left.label: No. He'll cause chaos.
left.reaction: He's coming anyway. With friends. Two thousand friends.

cards.text: Mayor. Trevor has led every lantern into the duck pond. On purpose. He says it was 'too beautiful to be on land'. Fine him?

right.label: Yes. Fine Trevor.
right.reaction: Barb fined a moth. He paid in dust. She's filed the dust.

left.label: No. It was beautiful.
left.reaction: It was beautiful. The ducks thought so. They're wearing lanterns now.

cards.text: Mayor, there are two thousand moths heading for the parade. The Bugle wants to run 'MOTH-AGEDDON'. Can we?

right.label: Yes. Run it.
right.reaction: Sold out. Everybody came to see the moths. The moths came to see the lanterns.

left.label: No. Don't scare people.
left.reaction: Marge ran 'MOTHS: FINE, PROBABLY'. Nobody believed it.

cards.text: (After the parade, Trevor has found one last lantern. It's yours. On your desk. He'd like to keep it. Forever.) Give it to him?

right.label: Yes. It's his.
right.reaction: He's sat on it every night since. He's named it 'Mayor'. You're touched.

left.label: No. It's council property.
left.reaction: He's sitting on your desk lamp instead. He's staring at you. Lovingly. Forever.

cards.text: (A traffic cone has entered the festival's fancy dress competition. It's Clive. He's come as a traffic cone.) Allow the entry?

right.label: Yes. Clive's in.
right.reaction: He's through to the final. Judges called his costume 'incredibly convincing'.

left.label: No. He's not in costume.
left.reaction: He's been moved. He's back. Holding a number. Nobody knows how.

cards.text: Mayor! Final round of fancy dress! It's Clive versus Gerald, who has come as a goose! I can't pick! You pick!

right.label: Clive.
right.reaction: Clive wins. Gerald honked for two hours. Then honked at Clive. Clive didn't flinch.

left.label: Gerald.
left.reaction: Gerald wins. He ate the rosette. Clive has moved one inch to the left. Ominous.

cards.text: Mayor! Clive the cone went viral! 'Cone enters contest, refuses to leave'! Can we sell Clive merch?

right.label: Yes. Cone merch.
right.reaction: Cone hats, cone mugs, cone cones. Sold out. Clive gets nothing. He seems fine with it.

left.label: No. He's private.
left.reaction: The Bugle ran 'CONE TOO HUMBLE FOR FAME'. Clive is more famous than ever.

cards.text: (The festival is over. Every cone in town has been put away. Except Clive. He's outside City Hall. Waiting.) Put him away?

right.label: Yes. Into storage.
right.reaction: You put him in the shed. In the morning, he was by your car. Facing you.

left.label: No. He's earned it.
left.reaction: Clive stays. A small plaque reads 'CLIVE. CONE. FESTIVAL CHAMPION (DISPUTED)'.

cards.text: (Since its disqualification, the cheese has been humming in the vault. Loudly. Doug says it's a protest song. It's catchy.) Reinstate it?

right.label: Yes. Reinstate it.
right.reaction: Reinstated. It won. By doing nothing. Again.

left.label: No. Rules are rules.
left.reaction: The humming is on every radio in town. It's number one.

cards.text: Mr Nutkins. The next town's Acornfest is a triumph. Yours is not. I'll sponsor you after all. At double the price. Agreed?

right.label: Yes. Double it.
right.reaction: Acornfest II. The signs are bigger. Mr Nutkins sits on the biggest one.

left.label: No. Still no.
left.reaction: He's sent you a postcard from the next town's festival. It's an acorn.

cards.text: (The bouncy castle is still in a cell. Still bouncing. Inspector Biscuit is bouncing too. It's the best day of his career.) Let him keep it?

right.label: Yes. Keep the castle.
right.reaction: The station is a bouncy castle now. Arrests are up. Everyone bounces in.

left.label: No. Release it.
left.reaction: Released. Biscuit watched it go. One small, sad bounce.

cards.text: (Lorraine's chip stall is on your roof now. The queue goes down your stairs. Your office is the waiting room.) Evict her again?

right.label: Yes. Evict her.
right.reaction: Evicted. She's moved into your car. It's a hatchback stall now.

left.label: No. Let her trade.
left.reaction: Your office is the busiest chip shop in town. You work in the queue.

cards.text: Linda. Professor Hoot held his quiz at noon. Asleep. In the library. Snoring. Everyone whispered the answers. Allow a night rematch?

right.label: Yes. Night rematch.
right.reaction: 3am. Hoot was magnificent. Nobody else was awake. He won.

left.label: No. Once is enough.
left.reaction: He's still asleep in the library. Linda has put a 'Quiet please' sign on him.

cards.text: (Toby is still sulking about the maypole. He's grown three feet in protest. Sideways. Into the high street.) Trim him?

right.label: Yes. Trim Toby.
right.reaction: Trimmed. He dropped every conker on the tree surgeon. One by one.

left.label: No. Go round him.
left.reaction: The high street goes round Toby now. He's very pleased with the new route.

objectives.text: Let the old ghosts into Wendy's haunted house
From day 4, get every group between 45 and 55 at once

low:people.title: Pelted with Marrow
low:people.text: The festival crowd turned on you. Bev led the charge. With vegetables. It was very well organised.

low:business.title: Festival Bankrupt
low:business.text: Every stall shut. Chad bought the field. You're a fairground ride now. You go round and round.

low:law.title: Escorted Off Site
low:law.text: Barb put a wristband on you that says BANNED. It won't come off. You've tried butter.

low:press.title: One-Star Review
low:press.text: The Bugle gave you one star out of five hundred. You're on page one, under 'Things To Avoid'.

low:treasury.title: Festival Fund Spent
low:treasury.text: The festival cost everything. Doug is paying the band in IOUs. The band is Randy.

high:people.title: Crowd-Surfed Away
high:people.text: The crowd loved you so much they crowd-surfed you out of the festival. Then out of town. You landed in the next county.

high:business.title: Sponsored
high:business.text: Chad sponsored you. You're now 'The Mayor, brought to you by Chad'. You have to say it every time you speak.

high:law.title: Head of Security
high:law.text: Barb made you head of festival security. You can't leave. You're in a hi-vis tabard. For ever.

high:press.title: Festival Celebrity
high:press.text: The Bugle made you the star of the festival. Photographers follow you everywhere. Even into the portaloo. Especially there.

rare:written_in.title: Written In
rare:written_in.text: You signed the blank page and became a character in Randy's memoir. Page 212. You're braver in the book. Everyone prefers that version.

rare:the_end.title: The End
rare:the_end.text: Randy wrote THE END. You live in the book now, as the hero. The town reads you at bedtime. Randy does the voices.

trap:allow_all.title: Allowed Everything
trap:allow_all.text: You tapped allow. The app spent the whole treasury on fireworks and launched them at once. It was beautiful. You're fired.

trap:stage_dive.title: Stage Dive
trap:stage_dive.text: You dived from the clock tower. The crowd parted, politely. You landed in Kevin. Kevin is fine. Your career is not.

trap:the_pie.title: The Pie
trap:the_pie.text: You ate the pie. You woke up on Thursday, in a hedge, wearing Bev's hat. You missed your own election. Bev voted for herself.

trap:held_rocket.title: Held the Rocket
trap:held_rocket.text: You held it. You saw the festival from above, then the next town, then a field. A cow elected you there. Not here.

trap:bridge.title: Under the Bridge
trap:bridge.text: The yacht fitted under the bridge. You didn't. You're on the bridge now, waving. The parade went on without you. So did the town.

trap:forever.title: Behind the Door Marked Forever
trap:forever.text: It said forever. It meant forever. You're a ghost now. Wendy shows you round. The pension is excellent.

trap:goat_ballots.title: Counted by Goat
trap:goat_ballots.text: You waited for the ballots to come back. Every readable one said GOAT. Pebbles is mayor. He has eaten the chain of office.

outw:people.title: Out-Voted by a Marrow
outw:people.text: Bev's marrow stood for election. It grew six feet during the count. It won by a landslide. It's still growing. So is its majority.

outw:business.title: Festival-Funded Out
outw:business.text: Chad sponsored the festival, the vote and the ballot box. The box said CHADFEST. Everyone voted for the box.

outw:law.title: Banned from the Festival
outw:law.text: Barb put a wristband on you that said OUT. It also bans you from your own office. It's waterproof. You've tried everything.

outw:press.title: Zero Stars
outw:press.text: The Bugle reviewed your week: zero stars. Then minus one. Then they gave the stars to Trevor the moth, who loves stars.

cliffhangers: Tomorrow: the Bin Lids have been rehearsing. Badly.
Tomorrow: forty pies. One of them is a cat.
Tomorrow: ten thousand rockets and one app.
Tomorrow: a yacht needs the high street.
Tomorrow: Wendy opens her doors. And her walls.
Tomorrow, the last day: a goat, a moth and a hole want your vote.
